In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytokine profile of Sicilian VL patients is not characterized by a clear-cut Th2 response as in mice.
IL-10, in addition to IFN-gamma and IL-4, plays an important role in the pathogenesis of active VL.
in Sicilian human patients with active VL, the cytokine profile does not clearly reflect a typical Th2 phenotype as observed in mice, and Th1-like and/or Th2-like cells are present and activated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the immune response to Leishmania donovanii is characterized by a Th1/Th2-like cytokine pattern in which both Th1- and Th2-like cytokine profiles are detectable, and that the Th1-like cytokine profile is predominant in the acute phase of VL, whereas the Th2-like cytokines are predominant after recovery.
in Sicilian VL patients the Th1 and Th2 cells are activated and produce cytokines in vitro and in vivo.
the cytokine profile in Sicilian patients is not clearly characterized as Th1 or Th2, and both Th2 and Th1 cells appear to proliferated and to be activated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-4 is not the major cytokine produced by T cells in human VL.
in vivo and in vitro studies of cytokines and mononuclear cells are useful in the evaluation of the immunological profile in patients affected with visceral leishmaniosis.
IL-10, which is a cytokine that is known to suppress the immune response, could be a useful marker for the follow-up of patients with visceral leishmaniosis.
